sources.title: nbformat v4 JSON schema (nbformat repo, branch main at capture)
sources.pin: branch main @ 2026-10-05 (unpinned commit; identity = capture sha256). Schema self-describes as 'Jupyter Notebook v4.5 JSON schema'; nbformat_minor minimum 5
sources.locator: definitions.code_cell.required = [id, cell_type, metadata, source, outputs, execution_count]; execution_count description: 'The code cell's prompt number. Will be null if the cell has not been run.'; output oneOf execute_result|display_data|stream|error; metadata.kernelspec required keys name/display_name. No field records kernel session identity or kernel liveness.
sources.applicability: Mechanism source for distinguishing displayed cell order, execution bookkeeping, and output association; the schema's absence of kernel-state fields is the documented gap our output-status model fills.

sources.title: JEP 62 — Cell ID Addition to Notebook Format (status: Implemented, 2020-09-25)
sources.locator: 'The id field in cells would always be required for any future nbformat versions (4.5+)'; motivation includes 'comparing a cell's output across multiple runs'; paste/copy collision rules; older formats auto-updated to 4.5.
sources.applicability: Cell identity is the join key between saved outputs, execution events, and provenance records; paste collision rules inform our invalidation semantics.

sources.title: DVC command reference: dvc status (docs source markdown)
sources.pin: branch main @ 2026-10-05 (unpinned commit; identity = capture sha256)
sources.locator: Local workspace states 'changed checksum' / 'always changed' / 'changed deps' / 'changed outs' with sub-states new|modified|deleted|not in cache; '--with-deps' example: editing code/featurization.py marks downstream stage matrix-train.p 'changed deps: modified: code/featurization.py'; import stages report 'update available' when the source changed; hashes recorded in dvc.lock or .dvc files.
sources.applicability: Independent precedent for content-hash dependency DAGs with explicit staleness reporting; the mechanism our output-status computation borrows (hash deps, diff, report reasons).

sources.title: DuckDB docs: Reading Faulty CSV Files (docs source markdown)
sources.pin: branch main @ 2026-10-05; rendered page canonical https://duckdb.org/docs/current/data/csv/reading_faulty_csv_files (site 'current' version observed as 1.5 on the rendered overview page)
sources.locator: Structural error types: CAST, MISSING COLUMNS, TOO MANY COLUMNS, UNQUOTED VALUE, LINE SIZE OVER MAXIMUM (default 2,097,152 bytes), INVALID ENCODING; ignore_errors option; store_rejects with reject_scans/reject_errors tables (columns include line, line_byte_position, column_name, error_type, csv_line, error_message); documented pitfall: 'the CSV Parser is affected by the projection pushdown optimization' so selecting only the valid column makes a CAST error disappear.
sources.applicability: Mechanism for quarantine-not-delete error handling, and a documented pitfall (projection-dependent error visibility) that motivates running contract validation over all declared columns.

sources.title: DuckDB docs: Samples (docs source markdown)
sources.locator: 'Samples are probabilistic, that is to say, samples can be different between runs unless the seed is specifically specified. Specifying the seed only guarantees that the sample is the same if multi-threading is not enabled (i.e., SET threads = 1).'; reservoir sampling gives exact row counts and is 'only recommended for small sample sizes'.
sources.applicability: Preview sampling design: seeded reservoir samples are repeatable under stated conditions but never constitute full-dataset properties.

sources.title: DuckDB docs: Concurrency (docs source markdown)
sources.pin: branch main @ 2026-10-05; page references DuckDB v1.5.2 (Quack remote protocol 'in beta stage as of DuckDB v1.5.2')
sources.locator: 'Read-write mode: one process can both read and write'; 'Read-only mode: multiple processes can read from the database, but no processes can write'; 'DuckDB handles concurrent database access requests using file locks. Exercise extra caution when accessing a DuckDB database file in a shared directory'.
sources.applicability: Concurrency/locking model: project-level single-writer policy; the SQL colleague opens project data read-only or on a copy.

sources.title: DuckDB docs: Combining Schemas (docs source markdown)
sources.locator: Default unifies by column position from the first file; union_by_name=true unifies by name and fills missing columns with NULL; note: 'Using the union_by_name option increases memory consumption.'
sources.applicability: Schema-evolution mechanism for datasets stored as multiple files whose schema drifts over time.

sources.title: DuckDB docs: Out-of-Memory Issues (docs source markdown)
sources.locator: 'Setting the memory limit lower than the default 80% can help prevent out of memory errors... because some of DuckDB's operations circumvent the database's buffer manager and thus they can reserve more memory than allowed by the memory limit'; guidance: SET threads lower, SET memory_limit to 50-60% of system memory, SET preserve_insertion_order = false for large reads/writes.
sources.applicability: 16 GB workstation envelope configuration and an explicit documented caveat that the memory limit is not a hard guarantee.

sources.title: DuckDB docs: Limits (docs source markdown)
sources.locator: 'Memory use | 80% of RAM | memory_limit | Note: This limit only applies to the buffer manager.'; 'Temporary directory size | unlimited | max_temp_directory_size'; 'DuckDB doesn't have a practical limit for the size of a single DuckDB database file... 15 TB+... checkpointing can be slower.'
sources.applicability: Bound declarations for large inputs: out-of-core temp space is available and unbounded by default; the memory cap is explicitly not a total-process guarantee.

sources.title: PEP 751 — A file format to record Python dependencies for installation reproducibility (Status: Final)
sources.pin: Status Final (resolution 31-Mar-2025); created 24-Jul-2024; replaces PEP 665; canonical spec on PyPA specs page (pylock.toml)
sources.locator: Header field-list (Status: Final); file name 'pylock.toml' or ^pylock\.[^.]+\.toml$; 'Currently, no standard exists to create an immutable record, such as a lock file, which specifies what direct and indirect dependencies should be installed into a virtual environment.'; installers consume without resolution.

sources.title: Frictionless Table Schema v1 (spec page)
sources.pin: Version 1; created 12 November 2012, updated 5 October 2021 (per page metadata); JSON Schema linked at /schemas/table-schema.json
sources.locator: 'physical and logical representation' concepts ('constraints should be tested on the logical representation... whereas a property like missingValues applies to the physical representation'); descriptor MUST contain ordered fields array; missingValues, primaryKey, foreignKeys; field types string|number|integer|... with formats.

capture.note: 32768-byte window of 70938-byte page; front matter, concepts, descriptor, and field descriptor sections observed.

sources.applicability: Existing interchange vocabulary for the dataset data contract (declared types, missing-value tokens, constraints); adopted selectively, not wholesale.

sources.title: Jupyter Server documentation: Security in the Jupyter Server
sources.pin: readthedocs 'latest' at capture; page metadata docsearch:version 2.22; last-modified 2026-09-15
sources.locator: 'Since access to the Jupyter Server means access to running arbitrary code, it is important to restrict access to the server.'

capture.note: 32768-byte window of 79569-byte page; the quoted security statement is in the observed window.

sources.applicability: Grounds the execution-boundary stance: the notebook server itself is an arbitrary-code executor, so isolation must come from the OS layer, not from the notebook tooling.

sources.title: JupyterLab user documentation: Notebooks (docs source markdown)
sources.locator: Trust section: 'JavaScript and HTML in notebooks created on other machines are not trusted, which results in sanitization of HTML and interactive outputs not being displayed until the notebook is explicitly trusted.'; 'Paste code cells without output' setting (pasting carries outputs by default otherwise); Cell ID exposed in Property Inspector.
sources.applicability: Evidence that outputs travel with documents independently of execution truth (paste behavior, trust gating), reinforcing that a saved output is not automatically reproducible.

sources.title: SQLite documentation: Write-Ahead Logging
sources.pin: Page last-modified 2026-09-11 (HTTP header); WAL available since SQLite 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) per page
sources.locator: Section 2 'How WAL Works': 'The original content is preserved in the database file and the changes are appended into a separate WAL file. A COMMIT occurs when a special record indicating a commit is appended to the WAL.'; Section 4: WAL file 'might be retained on disk after all connections to the database have been closed' if the last process exits uncleanly, and 'should be kept with the database if the database is copied or moved'; Section 2.3: synchronous=NORMAL omits per-commit sync (durability tradeoff).
sources.applicability: Precedent and mechanism for the project event store: crash-safe append-only log, readers-don't-block-writers, and copy-the-WAL-too rule for bundles.
